chunks: And ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

“If a man is overcome by sleep while he is in salat (prayer), then let him put down his head and sleep, for I fear for him that if he intends to say, ‘O Allah, admit me to Paradise,’ he may say instead, ‘O Allah, admit me to the Fire.’”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act in which the person is standing
key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: O Allah; vocative form used in du'a (supplication)
key_terms.النَّارَ: the Fire, the punishment one seeks refuge from
key_terms.النَّوْمُ: sleep that overtakes a person during worship
key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise, the desired abode asked for in supplication
key_terms.فَلْيَنَمْ: let him sleep; an instruction to stop and rest

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if sleep overcomes him during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs that when sleep overcomes a person during salat (prayer), he should sleep rather than continue in a state of impaired awareness. It highlights the importance of attentiveness in worship and warns that drowsiness may lead a person to utter words contrary to his intended du'a (supplication).
